newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian judge adjourns Prodi hearing until autumn.
newsitem.headline: Italian judge adjourns Prodi hearing until autumn.

text.p: A committal judge on Monday postponed a decision on whether to put Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi on trial, giving a panel of experts more time to examine financial aspects of the case.

Prodi faces allegations of abuse of office and conflict of interest over his role in the controversial privatisation of food company Cirio in 1993 when he was chairman of giant state industrial holding IRI.
A panel of accounting, commercial law and management experts was appointed by committal judge Edoardo Landi in March to look into the case.
They were supposed to present their findings on Monday but court officials said they had asked for an extension.

Public Prosecutor Giuseppa Geremia told reporters that Landi had given the panel until October 3 to file their report. She said it would be examined on October 27 with a decision expected on November 25.

Geremia alleges that Prodi and five other IRI board members at the time awarded an "unjust advantage" to a little known consortium called Fis.Vi, which bought Cirio for 310 billion lire ($182.7 million).
Prodi, who entered politics in 1995, was chairman of IRI for most of the 1980s and again for a year from May 1993.
He became prime minister at the head of a centre-left coalition in May 1995, and has suffered no evident political damage from the case, which does not involve allegations of personal enrichment.
He has said he will not resign if the case is sent to trial.
